boardNames: American Board of Pediatrics (ABP) — Pediatric Cardiology
boardStatus: Pediatric Cardiology is an ABP pediatric subspecialty with an ABP in-training, initial certification, and maintenance-of-certification content outline. It is not a separate degree conferred by this independent course.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABP (checked 2026-10-07) states that the ordinary route requires three years of full-time, broad-based pediatric cardiology fellowship in an ACGME-accredited U.S. or RCPSC-accredited Canadian program. General ABP criteria also require initial General Pediatrics certification and maintenance to take a subspecialty examination (subject to the stated pending-result circumstance), a valid unrestricted allopathic/osteopathic license in at least one U.S. jurisdiction/territory or Canada, program-director verification of training/competence/professionalism and scholarly activity, and a passing subspecialty certifying exam. For initial certification, ABP also states that required subspecialty training normally must have been completed within the previous seven years; the pediatric subspecialty examinations are offered every other year. Leaves, part-time training, prior credit, and the exceptional preapproved research fast-track/dual-training pathways have ABP-specific rules. This course, viewing videos, completing quizzes, clinical employment, an observership, or research alone does not establish any requirement, board eligibility, certification, license, or procedure privilege. Confirm current rules directly with ABP.

boardEligibilityNotice: Exact ABPN boundary, date checked 2026-10-07: applicant must be ABPN-certified in neurology or neurology with special qualification in child neurology by Dec. 31 before the exam; except for the expired 2005–2009 practice pathway, must document one year of ACGME-accredited Vascular Neurology fellowship begun after completing residency. boardEligibilityNotice: ABIM states that at application a physician must already be ABIM-certified in internal medicine; complete requisite ACGME/RCPSC/Collège des médecins du Québec accredited fellowship training; demonstrate clinical competence/procedural skills/professional behavior; hold a valid unrestricted unchallenged medical license; and pass the examination. boardStatus: This is an actual, distinct adult transplant-hepatology fellowship programme, not a generic directory category. Johns Hopkins’ programme page states that it is ACGME-accredited and one year long. The ABIM has a separate Transplant Hepatology Certification Examination; the January 2026 blueprint applies beginning with the Fall 2026 exam. The Hopkins directory entry’s “Accrediting Body: Non-Standard” field conflicts with the programme page, so the conflict is retained rather than silently resolved.
boardEligibilityNotice: Independent study does not provide fellowship appointment, ACGME credit, supervised clinical responsibility, procedural competence, a medical licence, ABIM/ABP eligibility, certification, MOC credit, or a guarantee of passing. For the ordinary ABIM route, the candidate must be previously ABIM-certified in gastroenterology at application, complete qualifying accredited training, hold a valid unrestricted and unchallenged licence, receive satisfactory programme verification, and pass the examination. ABIM describes 12 full-time clinical transplant-hepatology months after GI training; combined GI/TH has separate same-institution requirements. ABP eligibility is separate and requires current pediatric gastroenterology certification. Recheck the boards before application.
